LESSON 4
ISRAEL AS A REMINDER
Scripture Text: Jude 5
In this Scripture, Jude has introduced illustrations to remind the saints of the terrible
consequences that came upon ones in the past who did not believe. It is revealed to us
that the Lord does not hold people responsible for what they have never seen or
understood. The real danger to the saints is that after having known truth, walked in it,
and testified to it, they might let it become a reality of the past. This is just how apostasy
works. It moves people from the position they occupy in the truth to a totally different
position, while all the time they think they have not moved. That is why God prompted
Jude to bring up these Old Testament examples.
MEMORY VERSE: For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.
─Galatians 2:18
Stirring Our Remembrance
I will therefore put you in remembrance. This phrase reveals three things. One, knowledge is necessary for
there to be sin. James 4:17 tells us, “Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is
sin.” Jesus said, “If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth”
Two, man is a forgetful creature. God ordained that we constantly be reminded by the ministry. 2 Peter 1:12-
13 states: “Where-fore I will not be negligent to put you always in remembrance of these things, though ye
know them, and be established in the present truth. Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir
you up by putting you in remembrance.”
Three, being repetitious is the evidence of a good minister (see 1 Timothy 4:6). We should never become
weary with repetition, for just as it is in the military, repeated drills can mean the difference between life and
death.
The Great Deception
Though ye once knew this. This statement is proof that apostasy had truly made an inroad in Jude’s day and
was effective in its work even as it is today. Precious truths that were once carefully considered and lovingly
guarded were being viewed as excessive or fanatical and looked upon with disdain and scorn. 2 Peter 2:22
describes it this way: “But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own
vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.” A dog that returns to its own vomit
partakes of what once made it sick.
Apostates build again what they once destroyed. They are people who have moved to a past-tense experience
while making a present-tense profession, just as Saul did. Saul said, “Blessed be thou of the LORD: I have
performed the commandment of the LORD” (1 Samuel 15:13). He thought he had obeyed. The truth was, he
had disobeyed! This is the deception of apostasy.
Unbelief and Pride
How that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that
believed not. Here Jude was confronting those who had been moved by apostasy with the sobering reminder of
the Exodus account (see Numbers, Chapters 13-14). Israel was at the very borders of the Promised Land, at
Kadish-Barnea. Twelve spies had been sent out to survey the land. Of the twelve, ten brought back an evil report
© 2010 Church of God
Israel As A Reminder ─ Lesson 4
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS

that caused the people to murmur against Moses and Aaron. God heard their words and saw their unbelief. He
said, “Your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness” (Numbers 14:29). Of those who were twenty and older, only
Joshua and Caleb made it into Canaan.
We must know one thing to understand this example: the men who were corrupting the church then did not
regard themselves as enemies of the truth. They considered themselves to be advanced thinkers–a cut above the
ordinary saints. They were, by their own estimation, the spiritual elite. Jude chose this example of old Israel to
show that even if God has favored people with great privileges, they can still fall away into disaster. Consider
those in the past: Adam, Samson, Saul, Solomon, Judas, and Demas. We must be on constant watch against that
which could destroy us.
New Testament Warnings
The remembrance of what happened to old Israel haunted the minds of the New Testament ministers, who
were as responsible for leading God’s people as Moses was in the Exodus. The Israelites had been delivered
miraculously, just as the people in our study of Jude were genuinely delivered out of sin, but later on they were
destroyed. Why? Because of their unbelief. We must believe the report and obey the Gospel to stay saved. Those
with the sense of a superior spirituality do not feel they need to believe. They are moved by spirits with
teachings that are contrary to sound doctrine. This is why Paul said, “But with many of them God was not well
pleased . . . . Now these things were our examples” (1 Corinthians 10:5-6).
Jude as well as Paul was trying to awaken those who were falling prey to the enemy so that they would not
repeat the errors of the past. John Wesley warned, “Let none presume on past mercies, as if they were out of
danger.” 1 Corinthians 10:12 warns, “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” There
is no place of safe spiritual footing except the place of full obedience.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is a terrible thing to fall,
but it is worse yet to fall and think you are still standing!

LESSON 5
THE FALLEN ANGELS
Scripture Text: Jude 6
This verse has generated much confusion in the religious realm. Some believe the
word angels refers to celestial beings. They make reference to Genesis 6:2 and claim
that this is where angelic beings fell away. Others say Jude 6 refers to the supposed
revolt in Heaven, spoken of in Isaiah 14:12: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O
Lucifer.” However, Isaiah 14:16 lets us know that Lucifer was a man, not an angelic
being. If the word angels do not always represent celestial creatures, what angels did
Jude mean then when he wrote verse 6?
MEMORY VERSE: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation
wherewith ye are called.
─Ephesians 4:1
The Nature of This Epistle
Many commentators believe verse 6 must have an Old Testament literal fulfillment since verse 5 speaks of
old Israel and verse 7 speaks of Sodom and Gomorrah. However, it is necessary to understand the two-part
teaching style of this epistle. It is known as parallelism. In verse 4, Jude wrote of men who fostered apostasy in
his day, the first century. In verse 5, he used an example from the Old Testament. In verse 6, when he spoke of
angels, he was again referring to ones in the first century.
Notice the pattern: starting again in verse 7 and continuing through verse 16, every other reference goes from
the Old Testament example to the New Testament reality to show similarities or differences. In verse 6, he was
dealing with the New Testament reality.
Are There Sinning Angels?
The angels which kept not their first estate. When Peter dealt with this same truth, he said, “God spared
not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell” (2 Peter 2:4). These words are confusing to people in
false religion because they do not properly understand sin. There must be a power of choice to sin. James 4:17
says, “Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” The phrase “doeth it not”
portrays a power of choice, and the Scriptures do not teach that heavenly angelic beings have the power of
choice.
James 1:14 says that “every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Where
does “lust,” or desire, come from? 1 John 2:16 tells us: “For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the
lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Before one can sin, there must be
temptation. Temptation requires a fleshly, human nature. Celestial beings cannot be tempted to sin because they
do not have human natures. Therefore, these angels were not celestial beings.
The Greek word for angels is aggelos. It means “a messenger, a minister, or a pastor.” Jesus said in
Revelation 1:20, “The seven stars are the angels [aggelos] of the seven churches.” This text is dealing with
ministers or pastors who became instruments of apostasy, not celestial beings.
Jude and Peter were both speaking of a ministry that was angelic in the sense that it had been exalted “in
heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Ephesians 2:6). However, something happened. They kept not their first
estate. The Amplified Bible says that they “did not keep (care for, guard and hold to) their own first place of
power but abandoned their proper dwelling place.” What was “their proper dwelling place”? Psalm 90:1 says,
“L ORD , thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.” They left their proper abode when they left the
truth.
© 2010 Church of God
The Fallen Angels─ Lesson 5
www.GodsAcres.org

LESSON 5
A Fallen Ministry
Left their own habitation. When Jesus inspired the letter that represents the time period of A.D. 33-270, He
said, “Thou hast left thy first love” (Revelation 2:4). How did those ministers leave their “first love”?
According to Revelation 2:1-7, they were zealously practicing religion, but they had let it become a “form of
godliness” (2 Timothy 3:5). They failed to keep their experiences clear and sinned by substituting “the

means “One who is like God.” Some translations say that it means “Who is like God?” Two references to the
name Michael are in the Book of Daniel. In Daniel 10:21, it says, “Michael your prince,” and Daniel 12:1 says,

God’s glory, “the express image [copy] of his person.”

nearing the end of forty years of wandering in the wilderness, they met the elders of Moab and Midian, who

people . . . for I wot [know] that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed”
(Numbers 22:6).
One Aspect of the Error
The error of Balaam. When Balak’s representatives came and presented their request to Balaam, he initially
said the right thing. Numbers 22:8 reads, “Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as the L ORD
shall speak unto me.” He started out right because, before he made any decision or commitment, he prayed.
God told him, “Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed” (Numbers
22:12). After praying, Balaam told the men that the Lord refused to give him leave to go with them. That should
have been the end of it! However, Balak sent more princes who offered Balaam more honor and riches; then, he
committed the first aspect of his error.
The Greek word for error is the word plane, meaning “a wandering, a forsaking of the right path.” Balaam
had already prayed, and he knew the will of God, but he said, “Tarry ye also here this night, that I may know
what the L ORD will say unto me more” (Numbers 22:19). This was the fatal part of the error: he prayed again
hoping for a different answer to the same question. This is always a grave mistake! Malachi 3:6 states, “For I
am the L ORD , I change not,” and Psalm 119:89 says, “Forever, O L ORD , thy word is settled in heaven.”
The erring, or the “forsaking” of the right way, comes when one knows to do good but does not do it, then to
him it becomes sin (James 4:17). Balaam knew what was the good and right thing to do, but he left what he
knew was spiritually right to willingly follow what his flesh craved. Even so, God was as faithful to him.
Running for Reward
Ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward. One translation of this phrase says that they “abandon
themselves for the sake of gain.” Another translation says, “For the sake of gain they have rushed on headlong.”
Each translation shows the sad reality that once a person has forsaken the truth, the restraint of God’s grace is
not there anymore. The flesh takes hold of the individual with a dominant control, and that person rushes to
fulfill fleshly desires.

What would prompt people to do as Balaam did? 2 Peter 2:14-15 says: “. . . an heart they have exercised
with covetous practices; cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the
way of Balaam . . . who loved the wages of unrighteousness.” In verse 16 Peter called the Prophet’s actions
“madness.” Certainly, ones are mad to forfeit eternal reward for temporal gain.
Conditions of Today
In Jude and Peter’s day, people who had known the truth and been established in it were being duped by a
spirit that appealed to the flesh. 2 Peter 2:20 says, “For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world
through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the
latter end is worse with them than the beginning.”
In this day, we are having an evening-time apostasy much like that of the morning time. Many have been
able to get hold of God, hear from God, and take a clear stand on revealed truth; but over time, something has
happened. Just as Balaam was offered great honor and riches, the enemy has his agents who are trying to lure
the saints away from truth. They appeal to your sense of reason and make it seem reasonable for you to forsake
truth. You must be watchful that seducing spirits do not cause you to follow the flesh.
Many people today determine the stand they will take or the moves they will make by first deciding which
will gain them the greatest reward or be the most favorable for their flesh. They suppose “that gain is godliness
. . . . But godliness with contentment is great gain” (1 Timothy 6:5-6).
Haggai 1:6 says, “He that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” The more you put
into “a bag with holes,” the more it needs. This is exactly the way the flesh is. Once you begin to cater to it, you
can never satisfy it. You will only turn from fulfillment to frustration and become enslaved by trying to satisfy
fleshly passions and desires.

LESSON 12
THE ERROR OF BALAAM–PART 2
Scripture Text: Jude 11
As we review the text, we can see that each character so far has been involved in
religious activity. This clearly disproves the thought of, “If it is religious, then it must be
good.” Throughout history many things were done by numerous individuals in the name of
religion, but that certainly did not mean that they were right or that what they did was based
in the truth.
In the previous lesson, one part of the error of Balaam was that he prayed about whether
to go with Balak’s princes when he already knew the will of God. In this lesson, when Balaam could not curse
Israel, he conceived something worse with results that were more terrible and disastrous. This second episode is
what left its mark on Hebrew thought and teaching.
MEMORY VERSE: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of
death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.
─Romans 1:32
Balaam’s Ungodly Counsel
Psalm 1:1 states, “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly.” When Balaam saw that
he could not curse what God had blessed, he advised the women of Midian and Moab to seduce the Israelite men
and cause them to sin. He did this for reward. (The moves that were made in the morning time and the ones
being made today have come about from fleshly, carnal reasons and for temporal rewards, rather than from
divine guidance.) Balaam reasoned that if the Israelites would sin, then the Lord would have to punish them,
Balak’s purpose would be served, and he, Balaam, would be rich. Numbers 25:1-2 relates the result of that
plan: “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And
they called the people . . . and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.”
Three lessons can be learned from these verses. First, ungodly counsel affects not only the ones who receive
it but also those they have influence over. Second, close relationships can cause us to do something that we
normally would not do. Third, our affiliations with those whose worship and religion is different from the truth
can pull us into falsity.
A Spiritual Seduction
In Revelation 2:14, Jesus spoke of “the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumbling block
before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.” Why did Jude bring
up the thought of seduction in connection with apostasy? Because, just as seducers had worked under the
council of Balaam, there were spiritual seducers working in the first century.
Balaam used women to tempt Israel’s men to commit literal fornication. Satan uses seducing spirits to tempt
the saints to commit spiritual fornication. 1 Corinthians 6:18 admonishes us to “flee fornication.” Those who
took on seducing spirits in Jude’s day and left the truth and the true church but continued to profess to belong to
Christ were, in reality, engaging in spiritual fornication.
The Goal of Satan
Numbers 25:2 says that “the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.” Here the enemies’ original
intent is seen. It was to get the Israelites to come down to the level of worshiping “their gods.” This is the true
motive of apostates. They will woo you, love you, and show you much kindness; just as Solomon’s strange

LESSON 13
THE GAINSAYING OF CORE
Scripture Text: Jude 11
This lesson focuses on Core. His Hebrew name was Korah, which we are more
familiar with. He was the last of the three men, in this verse, to serve as an example of
the sad fate of apostates. We should not overlook the fact that all the statements in Jude
11 are in the past tense. In God’s sight, those who have been overcome by an apostate
spirit have already perished. Romans 4:17 says that God “calleth those things which be
not as though they were.” The fate of apostates is just as certain as the glorification of the
saints.
Memory Verse: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.
─2 Timothy 2:16
Who Was Core?
Why did Jude use Core? He was a Levite and a cousin to Moses (see Exodus 6:18-21). He had great
influence in the congregation. Along with two others, he started an insurrection, a rebellion, against Moses’
authority. Numbers 16:2 says that “they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two
hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown.”
This verse teaches that men who are highly revered and have tremendous influence, such as those in positions,
are the ones the enemy would like to use to work against the cause of God. Then, it teaches that you ought to be
extremely cautious about what you lend your influence and your name to.
The One Mediator
Numbers 16:3 says that Core charged Moses, saying, “Ye take too much upon you . . . wherefore then lift ye
up yourselves above the congregation of the L ORD ?” It is easy to see that religious jealousy was at the root of
this rebellion. Proverbs 6:34 says, “Jealousy is the rage of a man.” When one is overtaken by jealousy, he
becomes enraged, cruel, and does not exercise proper restraint.
Core rose up against Moses’ authority and God’s divine plan. Moses was a type of Christ; Aaron was a type
of the ministry. When those men opposed Moses and Aaron, they were in direct rebellion to God’s plan for a
mediator. 1 Timothy 2:5 states, “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ
Jesus.” They thought (as religion thinks today) that there could be many avenues, or mediators, but God had
chosen just one: Moses. In our day, Jesus Christ is our mediator–Mary cannot intercede for us and neither can a
priest or a preacher–only Christ!
Perishing in Apostasy
Perished in the gainsaying of Core. The word gainsaying comes from the Greek word antilogia. Anti
means “against”; logia means “the word.” Combined, they mean “against the word.” By studying verse 11, we
can see how apostasy worsens. Cain “ignored” the Word that had been spoken to him personally. Balaam
“subtly opposed” the Word that had been revealed to him. Core “openly rebelled” against the Word of God. His
name means “ice cold,” and he stood in cold-hearted defiance against God’s plan, God’s man, and God’s Word–
and he was punished for his actions.
How did he perish? Moses told him to gather all his men before God at the door of the tabernacle. What
happened? “There came out a fire from the L ORD , and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered
